verdict.tagline: Step into a feline adventure with cozy puzzles and short journeys.
not_for_you_if: you are prone to motion sickness

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial positive sentiment increases significantly as players progress past the opening hours.

cohorts.summary: Players encountering initial platforming and puzzles decide against recommending the game early on.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as heavily featuring platforming elements and puzzles.

citations.review_text: This blows.  I played for about an hour and a half and it is nothing more than a platform game. To top if off it totally screwed with my graphics settings.  As you can see by my specs, I'm not exactly playing with a tin pot PC, yet the game froze several times requiring me to reboot. Not my cup of tea.

I got really bored. I only played 1.3 hours and the last 30 minutes I've been forcing myself to play to "see it through" until I realized I have free will and don't have to put myself through this. The first 10 minutes was cute, but after going through the minimal and very guided platforming, minimal puzzles, the boring robot narrative, I realized this game is barely more than a walking simulator. If I had those expectations going in, I would've  maybe taken a different approach or played it while in a different mood.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players note the brief length and simple puzzles, though some report motion sickness and control issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is short, taking roughly between five and twelve hours to complete.

citations.review_text:
Fun little game that's worth playing for its incredible lighting and cyberpunk atmosphere. Traversing the environments as a slick cat is also really satisfying, particularly in hubs like The Slums and Midtown. The Slums in particular has a weirdly cozy atmosphere, and its densely packed, layered structure provides quite a bit of room for exploration, even though the overall area is actually pretty small.

The gameplay itself is fairly standard. Apart from the neat traversal and exploration, it's mostly platforming with several fetch quests and chase sequences, a few annoying stealth sections, and some easy puzzles thrown in. There are also collectibles in the form of badges, which you earn through small side quests or exploration, as well as memories hidden away in various nooks and crannies.

On a technical note, I also experienced occasional stuttering when performing certain actions or entering certain areas. From what I've heard, this is worse on PC than on consoles and is caused by shader compilation. It was mostly tolerable, but it seemed to happen fairly often in Midtown, which was a bit annoying. Aside from that, the game maintained a rock-solid framerate with low CPU and GPU usage, especially considering how good it looks.

One thing I really liked was the contrast between the cozy Slums and the eldritch, almost Lovecraftian environments in the Rooftops and Sewers. Some of those areas look like they're straight out of a horror game, and I really wasn't expecting that based on what I'd heard about the game.

The story itself is pretty bog standard, with robots imitating humans and replicating certain emotions, an evil corporation that wants to work everyone to death, and the usual class tensions between the rich and the poor. Seen it a million times already. My main motivation throughout the game wasn't really the story itself, but just the desire to escape the city and reach the outside to reunite with my friends.

One thing I didn't like at all was the end…
Adorable game that's nice and short. Great for players who want an entry-level video game. Press circle to meow!

This is a story driven game!
I enjoyed my little adventure with Stray. It managed to satisfy an interest story wise and a small thrill of adventure. It is a short game, story with basic exploration should take you around 8 hours mark with 100% can push you to 11/12 hours probably if you did not optimize from the start.

The Good:
- Story, I found myself asking questions and making theories about what is going on, was well made.
- World is beautiful and was well done, especially the cities, I found myself explorating the allies/roofs and trying to see everything.
- The concept of being a cat is strong, you can climb a lot of things and jump off places, it was decently done.

The Bad:
- Rushed story/encounters. In some situations when you meet and important figure or a scenario it feels so rushed, you can really feel it on the almost none existing chatter and the "skip".
- Most puzzles are very simple, maybe it's experience speaking but I don't remember a single one that was close to a challenge.
- This is an opinion but I would say the ending.
- The price is insane for an 8 hours gameplay, overpriced.


Fun and short game I would recommend this game but get it on an omega sale because it is overpriced like crazy.

claims.claim: Reviewers report experiencing motion sickness or nausea while playing.

citations.review_text: I was looking forward to playing this game but had to drop it. The graphics are pretty and the cat is cute, but the gameplay is dull and the camera made me nauseous.

Just finished playing and like all the other comments say, it's a beautiful game. You can tell a lot of heart went into making it. I'm primarily a cozy, puzzle gamer and this was a great cozy "last of us" but cats game.  My only critique is I got soooo motion sick while playing this game to the point I almost dnf. I just sat really far away from the computer lol. If possible, a way to turn on crosshairs or center dot would be so helpful. Other than that loved the world building, characters and scenery :)

My heart hurts, although it gave me quite the motion sickness, i love the game. the story line is not too confusing but i wish they would give a little bit more clue because cities here kinda feels like a maze

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering technical issues with keyboard and mouse controls during specific sections or chapters on PC.

citations.review_text:
For some INEXPLICABLE reason, the Devs decided to stop all mouse controls for the Dead End chapter (which is not even half way through the game!!!) So if you're on PC-you're screwed!  None of the keyboard or mouse controls are working!  I've been all over Google and Discord and tried various suggestions- NOTHING works!   You cannot fight off the Zurks at all because none of the keys seem to be working.  
Very upset and angry.

I'll start with the pros:
- really impressed with what the indie devs did visually here. On par with top tier studios

- I am the cat lady that this appeals to. I *love* getting to run around as a cat, knock things over, stick my head in a paper bag, scratch at doors to be let out, nuzzle against robots to get them to display heart faces and make happy robot chirps, and run through pool balls to make them roll around. The devs clearly know and love cats and it shows.

- As someone with hypermobile joints and dyspraxia that makes reaction timing hard, I really appreciate the auto-jumping. I know a lot of folks hate this, and it's a pro for me.

- I've read other reviews describe this game as hand-holdy and I think that's a fair complaint. For me, I like how obvious many of the aspects of the interactions and puzzle solving are because I'm not interested in this game to have a big think or a high stress combat experience. I just want to run around as a cat and have fun doing it.

Which brings me to my cons:
- Again, with the context that button mashing is murder on hypermobile joints and dyspraxia makes precision timing challenging, the combat runs against the zurks are game ruining for me. I am stuck in chapter 7 because after about 20 tries (and therefore having a clear understanding of the pathing) I can't get past them. I didn't time how much of my 3.9 hours of playtime was spent on the zurk sections and I wish I had that data. I just kept saying to myself 'this isn't fun' and finally quit in frustration.

- As others have mentioned, the gameplay might not be worth the price for those on tight budgets (with an acknowledgment that devs deserve to be paid and indie companies probably have a different funding structure than AAA companies? I'm not sure how all of that works). For me, I would have already returned this game if I had paid full price for it.

- Some have also mentioned that the puzzles are too simple, the exploration too railroaded, and this basically be…

A short little game that definitely exceeded my expectations; has a rather captivating story accompanied by beautiful and descriptive scenery. The overall gameplay is serviceable (as long as you use a controller, cause the keybinds on keyboard are god awful) as it comes with chases, puzzles, and some light exploration. It's easy by nature, but that doesn't necessarily make it bad by any means. The main selling point is for sure the story, and it is one worth experiencing to say the least. Neat little game, strong 8.8/10

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players find the puzzles thoughtful yet accessible, while noting the brief overall length.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game's overall length feels too short.

citations.review_text: This game has it all. The movement feels slick and satisfying, the story is interesting, and the sound/environment designs are awesome. All the side missions you can do are also memorable along to the story, and overall the game is very immersive and makes for a great experience. If I were to have any sort of quarrel, it is that the game is a little too short but thats also what makes it such a memorable experience.
Interesting world and environment but the gameplay feels too short.
Loooved this game, the story a little short (found out later how much game time there is for main story) but everything else in the game amazing!!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the puzzles as moderately challenging without being overly difficult or requiring outside solutions.

citations.review_text: Such a lovely game! Atmospheric and beautiful settings to explore. An open-world exploration feeling but within a series of fairly contained spaces. Puzzles are challenging enough that you have to think, go back and review clues, or retrace your steps but not so hard that you have to look anything up (I was able to complete the game without feeling frustrated enough to look up any solutions). The game has a natural flow that guides you to what is next. Highly recommend this game!

This game is by far the best game I've played in 2026! I didn't expect a game, where the playable character is a cat, to have such a rich story. The world is absolutely beautiful. Every character is developed to perfection. The puzzles are just the right amount of challenging. Suspenseful moments are broken up with cute cat naps. I loved this game and I'll probably go back to collect all the achievements, which I rarely ever do. 10/10 would recommend!

Stray completely stole my heart. What I loved most about this game is that there are no humans. It's just robots, cats, and this beautiful world full of mystery. I don't know why, but that made the game feel so special to me. The robots have so much personality, and I became attached to many of them during my journey. The world is absolutely beautiful. The neon lights, the colors, the rainy streets, and all the small details made me stop so many times just to look around. Every area feels unique and full of life. The story is simple but emotional. I loved discovering the world little by little instead of having everything explained to me. It made me feel curious and excited to keep exploring. The soundtrack is also amazing and fits the atmosphere perfectly. It made some moments feel peaceful and others feel emotional. The puzzles are fun and not too difficult. They were just enough to keep me engaged without becoming frustrating.
And of course, playing as a cat is sooo cutee <3 Meowing for no reason, taking little naps, scratching things, and knocking objects off shelves made me smile every time. I never thought I could get so attached to a little orange cat.
I've finished Stray several times already, and I still love it every time I play. That's very rare for me. There is just something magical about this game that keeps bringing me back.
I genuinely can't think of a single thing I didn't enjoy.
Beautiful, cozy, emotional, and unforgettable. I fell in love with this dystopian world, its robots, and its little orange cat. One of my favorite games ever. ❤️🐾✨
